title: WPMS/2197/2011 of VIKAS SHARMA Vs MUSSOORIE DEHRADUN DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY AND ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 2197 (MS) of 2011
Vikas Sharma. ÖÖÖPetitioner.

Versus
Mussoorie Dehradun Development Authority
& others. ÖÖ.Respondents.
Present:
Mr. Aman Rab, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. R.C. Arya, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Rahul Consul, Advocate for MDDA.
Honíble Alok Singh, J (Oral).
Writ petition was dismissed for non prosecution on
24.02.2014. Restoration application to restore the writ petition was
moved on 13.03.2014. It is stated in the affidavit filed along with
restoration application that when the matter was called out on
24.02.2014, counsel for the petitioner was busy in another court,
therefore, he could not appear before the Court, consequently, writ
petition was dismissed for non prosecution.
Mr. Rahul Consul, Advocate appearing for respondent
nos. 1 to 3/ MDDA submitted that order dated 24.02.2014 may be
recalled and writ petition may be restored to its original number but
the same may be heard finally today itself.
For the reasons stated, restoration application no. 92 of
2014 is allowed. Order dated 24.02.2014 is hereby recalled. Writ
petition is restored to its original number.
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties,
present writ petition was taken up and heard finally and is being
disposed of by this judgment.
Present writ petition is filed assailing the order dated
28.02.2011 passed by MDDA whereby explanation was called from
the petitioner as to why constructions raised by him in village

2
Dudhali near Crew Station, Mussoorie be not demolished and
further directed to seal the construction, in question.
Initially, ground taken by the petitioner was that village
Dudhali did not fall within the territorial jurisdiction of MDDA,
therefore, no map was required to be submitted before the MDDA
for sanction. Consequently, show cause notice as to why building be
not demolished and order sealing the building were without
jurisdiction.
This Court vide order dated 22.04.2011 passed in WPMS
No. 727 of 2011 was pleased to direct the MDDA to decide the
representation of the petitioner challenging jurisdiction of MDDA.
MDDA vide order dated 26.09.2011 (Annexure No. 10 to the writ
petition) was pleased to hold that construction site is within
municipal limits of MDDA, therefore, construction raised by the
petitioner fell within the territorial jurisdiction of MDDA. Order
dated 26.09.2011 is also under challenge in the present writ petition.
Mr. Aman Rab, Advocate appearing for the petitioner,
on the instructions of Mr. Vikas Sharma, petitioner, present in
person before the Court, submitted that petitioner could not submit
the map for sanction before the MDDA under the bona fide belief
that village Dudhali did not fall within the territorial limits of
MDDA. He further contends that map for sanction of the
construction already raised shall be submitted before the MDDA
within four weeks from today along with an application seeking
compounding of the constructions, whereupon MDDA should pass
appropriate order in accordance with law within reasonable time.
Mr. Rahul Consul, Advocate appearing for MDDA,
submits that let petitioner moves proper application seeking
compounding along with the map within four weeks from today, as
stated by Mr. Aman Rab, Advocate for the petitioner and thereafter,
appropriate decision shall be taken thereon in accordance with law

3
preferably within 90 days thereafter. Decision, so taken, shall be
communicated to the petitioner.
Mr. Rahul Consul, Advocate for MDDA, in all fairness,
for which he is known at Bar, submits that if any lacuna is observed
by the MDDA either in the compounding application or in the map,
the same shall be communicated to the petitioner forthwith so that
he may rectify the same within the time given by the MDDA.
Application seeking compounding and sanction of map shall not be
rejected on any hyper technical ground.
In view of the above, present petition is disposed of
with liberty to the petitioner to move appropriate application
seeking compounding and sanction of map within four weeks from
today whereupon appropriate decision shall be taken by the MDDA
within 90 days thereafter.
Meanwhile, no demolition shall be carried out. It goes
without saying that if map is sanctioned by the MDDA, MDDA shall
pass order de-sealing the property.
Petition as well as CLMA No. 4029 of 2014 and IA No.
1707 of 2014 stand disposed of.
(Alok Singh, J.)
 09.05.2014
SKS
